title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #19

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word has the long vowel /ɑː/? (1 mark)
   A. coin
   B. light
   C. burn
   D. market

2. A new idea in a composition begins (1 mark)
   A. with a question mark
   B. in the same sentence
   C. in a new paragraph
   D. in capital letters

3. Which is a linking word that shows something happened at the end? (1 mark)
   A. next
   B. first
   C. then
   D. finally

4. Which word best describes Neema in the passage? (1 mark)
   A. honest
   B. lazy
   C. rude
   D. greedy

5. We answer comprehension questions best in (1 mark)
   A. drawings only
   B. full sentences
   C. one letter
   D. numbers only

6. Which is correct spelling? (1 mark)
   A. alot of
   B. a lot of
   C. allot of
   D. a lott of

7. In 'bandage', the stress is on (1 mark)
   A. neither
   B. the first syllable
   C. the second syllable
   D. both syllables

8. Which word starts with the cluster 'sn'? (1 mark)
   A. stop
   B. stitch
   C. snake
   D. treatment

9. A visual is something we (1 mark)
   A. taste
   B. understand by looking at it
   C. smell
   D. hear only

10. What punctuation mark follows the greeting 'Dear Achieng'? (1 mark)
   A. A colon
   B. A question mark
   C. A comma
   D. A full stop

11. Which word has the short sound /ʊ/? (1 mark)
   A. fruit
   B. moon
   C. cook
   D. spoon

12. What is a good habit for a listener? (1 mark)
   A. Play with things
   B. Look away
   C. Talk while others speak
   D. Look at the speaker and do not interrupt

13. Which material gives you news? (1 mark)
   A. A map key
   B. A dictionary
   C. A story book
   D. A newspaper

14. What is the comparative of 'bad'? (1 mark)
   A. worst
   B. worse
   C. badder
   D. more bad

15. An adjective is a word that (1 mark)
   A. joins sentences
   B. describes a noun
   C. names a person
   D. shows an action

16. In the safety dialogue, why did the message say 'You have won a prize'? (1 mark)
   A. To reward Neema
   B. To help her homework
   C. To teach spelling
   D. It was a trick to steal information

17. Quantifiers: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. I do not have some money.
   B. I do not have any money.
   C. I do not have many money.
   D. I do not any have money.

18. What does the proverb 'Look before you leap' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Always look at your feet
   B. Think carefully before you act
   C. Jump as high as you can
   D. Do not go outside

19. Which time word usually goes with the present progressive? (1 mark)
   A. in 2010
   B. last night
   C. at the moment
   D. yesterday

20. Which sentence is in the present progressive? (1 mark)
   A. The teacher marked our books.
   B. The teacher had marked our books.
   C. The teacher marks our books.
   D. The teacher is marking our books.

21. What does it mean to read in phrases? (1 mark)
   A. To read backwards
   B. To read only the first word of each line
   C. To read groups of words that go together
   D. To read one letter at a time

22. Which sentence is a good ending for a story? (1 mark)
   A. And the sun.
   B. Farm.
   C. We caught the goat together, and I was tired but proud.
   D. Then a goat.

23. Which of these is a nonverbal cue that shows confidence? (1 mark)
   A. Standing straight and looking at your audience
   B. Looking at the floor
   C. Hiding your face
   D. Turning your back

24. What is a virus? (1 mark)
   A. A sharp tool
   B. A tiny germ that can make people ill
   C. A type of food
   D. A kind of medicine

25. Where does an adverb of frequency such as 'always' usually go in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Before the capital letter
   B. Inside a word
   C. At the end after a full stop
   D. Before the main verb

26. Which pair differs in the sounds /s/ and /ʃ/? (1 mark)
   A. go and no
   B. sea and she
   C. sit and seat
   D. live and leave

27. What does 'sanitation' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of food
   B. Clean toilets, drains and waste systems that protect health
   C. A type of shoe
   D. A game

28. According to the text, when should we wash our hands? (1 mark)
   A. Never with soap
   B. Only when we see dirt
   C. After using the toilet
   D. Only on Sundays

29. Which sentence has a comma before 'but' joining two full sentences? (1 mark)
   A. I was tired but I finished sweeping,
   B. I was tired but, I finished sweeping.
   C. I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   D. I was, tired but I finished sweeping.

30. Which word has the sound /aʊ/? (1 mark)
   A. hot
   B. cat
   C. bell
   D. crowd

31. What does it mean to read a poem interpretively? (1 mark)
   A. To count the words
   B. To copy it
   C. To think about its meaning and feelings and show them in your voice
   D. To read it silently in one second

32. In a comic, what do speech bubbles show? (1 mark)
   A. The author's name
   B. The price
   C. The page number
   D. What the characters say

33. Which question word asks about a thing or an action? (1 mark)
   A. whose
   B. what
   C. where
   D. when

34. Which is the best question for the answer 'In the school hall'? (1 mark)
   A. Whose hall is it?
   B. Who practised?
   C. Where did they practise?
   D. When did they practise?

35. Which of these is a homophone pair? (1 mark)
   A. big and large
   B. hot and cold
   C. their and there
   D. run and walk

36. Which word has a double r? (1 mark)
   A. library
   B. tomorrow
   C. necessary
   D. beautiful

37. Which word has the short vowel /ʌ/? (1 mark)
   A. sport
   B. mother
   C. floor
   D. door

38. In which word is the letter b silent? (1 mark)
   A. bus
   B. debt
   C. baby
   D. bag

39. Which page of a magazine lists the articles and their page numbers? (1 mark)
   A. The advert page
   B. The contents page
   C. The cover
   D. The comic page

40. Which word has a double consonant? (1 mark)
   A. paper
   B. later
   C. letter
   D. river

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Replace each plain word with a better describing word: nice room, dirty clothes, good smell. Write the new phrases. (3 marks)

42. Create a short puzzle with four clues whose answers are irregular plurals. (4 marks)

43. Explain the difference between 'good' and 'well'. Give one sentence for each. (4 marks)

44. Explain three uses of the comma with an example for each. (5 marks)

45. Write about 60 words about these pictures: (1) A boy plants a seed. (2) He waters it every day. (3) A tall plant grows. (5 marks)

46. Correct the spellings: peple, libary, beutiful. (3 marks)

47. Write three yes/no questions about keeping the compound clean. (3 marks)

48. Fill in much or many: (a) How ___ eggs? (b) How ___ sugar? (2 marks)

49. Describe how to make the sounds /f/ and /v/ and say how they are different. Give one example pair. (4 marks)

50. Draw a mind map in words: put 'Keeping Fit' in the centre and give four branches. (4 marks)

51. Give three words with silent letters and name the silent letter in each. (3 marks)

52. Use when, where, who and whose in four questions about a sports day. (4 marks)

53. State three materials you can read for pleasure. (3 marks)

54. Rewrite in the past tense: 'Baraka types a message and clicks Send.' (2 marks)

55. Describe the five-finger test for choosing a book. (4 marks)

56. Explain how you can feel the difference between /t/ and /d/ using your throat. (2 marks)

57. Give one direct question and one indirect question about a story of a birthday party. (3 marks)

58. Replace the second mention with a pronoun: 'Neema saw the bridge. Neema liked the bridge.' (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — market
   Market has /ɑː/ in its first syllable.

2. C — in a new paragraph
   Each paragraph holds one idea.

3. D — finally
   Finally introduces the last event.

4. A — honest
   She returned the purse and refused a reward.

5. B — full sentences
   Full sentences show that we understand.

6. B — a lot of
   A lot is two words.

7. B — the first syllable
   We say BAN-dage.

8. C — snake
   Snake starts with s and n.

9. B — understand by looking at it
   Pictures, signs, maps and videos are visuals.

10. C — A comma
   A comma follows the greeting.

11. C — cook
   Cook has /ʊ/.

12. D — Look at the speaker and do not interrupt
   Good listeners give attention.

13. D — A newspaper
   Newspapers report news.

14. B — worse
   Bad, worse, worst.

15. B — describes a noun
   Adjectives describe nouns.

16. D — It was a trick to steal information
   The message asked for her name and address.

17. B — I do not have any money.
   Use any in negative sentences.

18. B — Think carefully before you act
   It advises us to think before we do something.

19. C — at the moment
   'At the moment' shows an action happening now.

20. D — The teacher is marking our books.
   Is + verb-ing shows an action happening now.

21. C — To read groups of words that go together
   Chunking words into phrases makes reading smoother.

22. C — We caught the goat together, and I was tired but proud.
   An ending tells how the story finishes and how people felt.

23. A — Standing straight and looking at your audience
   Posture and eye contact show confidence.

24. B — A tiny germ that can make people ill
   A virus is a tiny germ.

25. D — Before the main verb
   For example: 'I always brush my teeth.'

26. B — sea and she
   'Sea' has /s/ and 'she' has /ʃ/.

27. B — Clean toilets, drains and waste systems that protect health
   Sanitation protects health by keeping waste away.

28. C — After using the toilet
   The text lists after using the toilet, before eating and more.

29. C — I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   A comma comes before but when joining two full sentences.

30. D — crowd
   'Crowd' has the diphthong /aʊ/, as in 'cow'.

31. C — To think about its meaning and feelings and show them in your voice
   Interpretive reading brings out meaning and feeling.

32. D — What the characters say
   Speech bubbles hold spoken words.

33. B — what
   'What' asks about things, ideas and actions.

34. C — Where did they practise?
   The answer names a place.

35. C — their and there
   They sound the same but are spelt differently.

36. B — tomorrow
   'Tomorrow' is t-o-m-o-r-r-o-w.

37. B — mother
   'Mother' has the short /ʌ/.

38. B — debt
   'Debt' is said 'det'.

39. B — The contents page
   The contents page shows where to find each article.

40. C — letter
   'Letter' has a double t.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: bright, tidy room; muddy, crumpled clothes; fresh smell.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have two of these and I walk on them: feet. You chew with these: teeth. Small animals that squeak: mice. Grown-up females: women.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clue with a correct answer.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: 'Good' is an adjective and describes a noun: She is a good singer. 'Well' is an adverb and describes a verb: She sings well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for each sentence.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: In lists: rice, beans and cabbage. After yes or no: Yes, I can. When addressing a person: Mama, come here. Also before but/so between sentences.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use and example (max 5 including quality of examples).

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: One morning, Musa planted a seed in the garden. Every day he watered it. After some weeks, a small green shoot appeared. At last, a tall plant grew and Musa was proud.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for beginning, order, linking words, past tense, punctuation and length.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: people, library, beautiful
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Do you sweep the compound? Is the bin covered? Can we plant a tree?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) many (b) much
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Touch the top teeth to the lower lip and blow. /f/ is whispered and /v/ is voiced with a buzz. Example: fan and van.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mouth position, 1 mark for /f/ whispered, 1 mark for /v/ voiced, 1 mark for the pair.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Centre: Keeping Fit. Branches: exercise, healthy food, sleep, clean water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the centre and 1 for each branch.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: knee (k), debt (b), honest (h).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word with its silent letter.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: When is sports day? Where is it held? Who is the guest of honour? Whose team is winning?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Story books, poems, magazines, comics, newspapers (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Baraka typed a message and clicked Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each verb.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Open the book at a page and read it. Hold up a finger for every word you do not know. Five fingers means too hard; one to three fingers is a good fit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reading a page, 1 for counting unknown words with fingers, 1 for what five fingers means, 1 for what one to three fingers means.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put your fingers on your throat and say the sounds. You feel a buzz with /d/ because it is voiced, but no buzz with /t/, which is whispered.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the buzz with /d/, 1 mark for no buzz with /t/.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Direct: What time did the guests arrive? Indirect: Why do you think the girl was excited?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each question and 1 mark for correct types.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neema saw the bridge. She liked it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for she and 1 mark for it.
